samples.summary: Shared spreadsheet viewer still writes presence (and can write axis order) to the CRDT — the one read-only mount this change did not guard
samples.evidence:
This change flips the Yorkie auth webhook to enforce-by-default and, on that basis, adds `readOnly` guards to every client-side local write a share-link viewer could make: `board-view.tsx:595` (selection presence), `pdf-collab.tsx:134` (activePage presence) and `slides-view.tsx:1137` (broadcast). The spreadsheet mount was missed.

`SharedDocumentLayout` mounts `<SheetView tabId=... readOnly={readOnly} />` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:283), and `sheet-view.tsx:1012` constructs `new YorkieStore(doc, tabId)` unconditionally — there is no read-only store variant on this path (`ReadOnlyStore` in packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts is a separate class only exported, never wrapped around `YorkieStore`).

- packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:86 — the constructor itself does `this.doc.update((_, p) => p.set({ activeTabId }))`, so a viewer produces a local change the moment the sheet mounts.
- packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:628 — `updateSelection()` publishes presence on every selection change; it is called unconditionally from the model (`packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3045` and `:3058`), with no `readOnly` gate anywhere in between.
- packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:657 — `ensureAxisOrder()`, invoked from the same selection path (`sheet.ts:3029`), is a genuine **root** write when a selection reaches past current axis coverage.

By the diff's own reasoning (see the comments it adds at board-view.tsx:595 and pdf-collab.tsx:129), a local change is carried by the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the now-default-enforcing webhook refuses for a share-link `viewer` — wedging the viewer's own sync. For sheets this happens at mount, before the visitor touches anything.

samples.summary: `shareTokenImageUploader` does not satisfy the notes `UploadImage` contract, so a share-link editor's failed image upload fails silently
samples.evidence:
The new layout hands `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` straight to `NotesView`'s `uploadImage`. That function is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15) and **throws** on failure. The notes contract is different: `UploadImage = (file) => Promise<string | null>` where `null` means "the host already reported this to the user" (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:26, and the prop doc at packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx:46). The engine's rejection path only does `console.error('Image upload failed', err)` and drops the placeholder (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:179-190) — no toast.

The workspace route wraps its uploader exactly to satisfy this: `notes-detail.tsx:208-227` catches, toasts, and returns `null`. The shared route does not, so an editor-role visitor whose upload fails (oversize, unsupported type, 403) sees the placeholder vanish with no explanation.

samples.summary: Design doc and two package comments still assert the old "shadow mode by default" contract that this change reverses
samples.evidence:
`isYorkieAuthEnforced` now makes enforcement the default, but several out-of-diff sites still document the opposite:
- docs/design/sharing.md:208 — "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode", and sharing.md:233 repeats it ("with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there").
- packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 — "ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary". The new `readOnlyNoteStore` explicitly corrects this claim for notes; the docs twin it mirrors was left stating it.
- packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413 — same stale premise.
- Even inside this change, packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:445 adds a new comment saying "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default", contradicting the file's own new store wrapper and `yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts`.

Nothing breaks, but the security rationale readers rely on now points the wrong way (and the top-level-docs link check only validates backticked paths, not claims).

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate at every cited location. The change makes the Yorkie auth webhook enforce by default (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29) and adds readOnly gates to presence writes in board-view.tsx:601 and pdf-collab.tsx:134, both commented that a presence doc.update() rides the next PushPull with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a share-link viewer (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:288-324 confirms verb derivation and explicitly notes a local change on load is denied). The shared spreadsheet mount is not gated: shared-document.tsx:181/283/1024 mounts SheetView with readOnly for a viewer, but sheet-view.tsx:1012 constructs YorkieStore unconditionally (readOnly is only forwarded to initialize at :1017), and yorkie-store.ts:86-88 writes presence in the constructor at mount. updateSelection (yorkie-store.ts:628) and the root-mutating ensureAxisOrder (yorkie-store.ts:666) are reached from packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3029/3045/3058 via syncSelectionToPresence, and sheet.ts contains no readOnly concept at all (grep: no matches); readOnly in the sheets package only gates edit paths in the view layer. ReadOnlyStore is only used by datasource-view.tsx:29 and lakehouse-view.tsx:40, never for the shared Yorkie sheet path. This is a guard-with-a-bypass in a file the diff did not touch — in lane, and major (viewer sync wedged at mount, plus a possible root write).

finding.summary: PDF presence publish is not gated on `readOnly`, so a viewer share link still makes a local `doc.update` — the exact rw-PushPull denial the diff removes from `initialRoot` in the same file
finding.evidence: `PdfCollabStateProvider.onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r, p) => p.set({ activePage: pageIndex }))` unconditionally (pdf-collab.tsx:124-128); it is wired to page scroll for every mount, including `SharedPdfLayout`'s `readOnly = resolved.role === 'viewer'` (shared-document.tsx:699-712). The diff's own reasoning at pdf-collab.tsx:191-202 is that any local change is carried by the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the webhook refuses for a viewer — and this PR makes enforcement the DEFAULT. The notes half of the same PR neuters `setLocalSelection` for precisely this reason (`packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts`: "publishing a caret is a `doc.update` like any other"). So a viewer scrolling a shared PDF gets its sync denied while the seeding path next to it was fixed. Same class, unchecked, in slides (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:2751`) and board (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/yorkie-board-store.ts:567`), neither of which has a read-only store wrapper the way docs and now notes do.

verdict.reason: The finding's core presence claim is false. It asserts `PdfCollabStateProvider.onActivePageChange` does `doc.update((_r,p) => p.set({activePage}))` UNCONDITIONALLY. In fact pdf-collab.tsx:134 reads `if (readOnly || !doc || pageIndex === lastPageRef.current) return;` — `readOnly` is the first condition in the early return, directly guarding the `doc.update` on line 136. The comment at pdf-collab.tsx:122-131 also states verbatim the exact rationale the reviewer claims is missing (presence publish is a doc.update carried by the next PushPull with verb `rw`, refused for a share-link viewer). The guard is correctly wired for the viewer path the finding names: shared-document.tsx:699 computes `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, passes it at :709 to PdfCollabProvider, which forwards to PdfCollabStateProvider at pdf-collab.tsx:217. Because the guard lives inside `onActivePageChange` itself (the function put on context at :162), every consumer including the sole PdfViewer wiring at :318 gets the guarded version — there is no unguarded second entry point. Both trailing "same class, unchecked" claims are also false: slides guards at slides-view.tsx:1137 (`if (readOnlyMount) return;`) and board guards selection at board-view.tsx:601 (`if (readOnly) return;`), while the board cursor publisher that calls updatePresence at :521 is only reachable through listeners attached under `if (!readOnly)` at board-view.tsx:538. No bypass exists at any of the three cited locations.
